classification.difficultyReason: Draw the described figures, recognise equal sides or radii, and combine equal base angles with straight-angle or triangle-angle sums.

content.prompt: In each part, draw a diagram and mark equal intervals and the given sizes of angles.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$. Mark $D$, a point on $BC$ on the opposite side of $C$ from $B$. If $\angle ACD=110^\circ$, calculate the size of $\angle ABC$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=180^\circ-110^\circ\\\angle ACB&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line at $C$ sum to $180^\circ$.

$\angle ABC=\angle ACB=70^\circ$ because the base angles of isosceles $\triangle ABC$ are equal ($AB=AC$).

children.label: b
children.prompt: $P$ and $Q$ are points on a circle with centre $O$ such that $\angle POQ=56^\circ$. Calculate the size of $\angle OPQ$.

answer.worked:
$OP=OQ$ because they are radii of the same circle. Hence $\angle OPQ=\angle OQP$ because the base angles of isosceles $\triangle OPQ$ are equal.
$$\begin{align*}\angle OPQ+\angle OQP&=180^\circ-56^\circ\\\angle OPQ+\angle OQP&=124^\circ\\\angle OPQ&=124^\circ\div2\\\angle OPQ&=62^\circ\end{align*}$$
